purpose: Measure whether observer process records preserve exact process incarnations, parent-child lineage, lifecycle ordering, and event-loss integrity against an independent supervisor oracle.
non_goals: process argument or environment secret capture
authentication of oracle or observer authors
thread-level task lineage and CLONE_THREAD accounting; v1 does not claim complete task-graph coverage

identity_contract.pid_reuse_policy: same PID with different start_time_ticks is a new process instance; same PID and same start_time_ticks is ambiguous/duplicate within a single lineage and must be rejected
identity_contract.namespace_policy: PIDs from different PID namespaces are never joined, even when numeric PID and start_time_ticks match
identity_contract.time_policy: monotonic nanoseconds for event ordering; raw /proc start_time_ticks are identity material, not wall-clock timestamps
identity_contract.pidfd_policy: independent supervisor should use pidfd/CLONE_PIDFD where practical to retain a kernel reference to each child lifecycle; fallback /proc start_time_ticks must be separately stratified and disclosed The oracle should retain each pidfd while the task is alive; pidfd does not itself discover arbitrary descendants or exec events.

comparison_arms.description: Join processes by numeric PID alone; expected to mismerge PID reuse and namespace collisions.
Use PID plus /proc/PID/stat start-time ticks, host boot identity and PID namespace identity.
Independent supervisor retains pidfd references (or CLONE_PIDFD where available) and records wait/exit outcomes, alongside namespace-scoped process identities.
Use Falco kernel syscall events and its supported process-related event stream; retain native drop counters and exact configuration.
Use Tetragon process_exec/process_exit records, parent metadata and exec_id; record version, policy and event export path.
Consume observer process/event receipt without an independent process graph or event-set reconciliation.
Reconcile observer process graph and lifecycle event stream against a separate supervisor oracle, sequence counters and scoped identity.

metrics.definition: Fraction of supervisor-observed process instances present with exact PID and start_time_ticks under the matching boot/PID-namespace/run/task/attempt scope.
Fraction of reported parent edges that exactly match the independent supervisor graph, with no orphan or cross-lineage parent.
Fraction of controlled PID-reuse cases represented as distinct process instances rather than merged by numeric PID.

Fraction of expected root_start/fork/clone/vfork/exec/exit event occurrences represented exactly once for the correct process instance; a process may have multiple distinct exec events, while birth and exit cardinalities remain strict.
Fraction of injected per-source sequence gaps and duplicates detected and made non-promotable.
Count of runs accepted as complete despite nonzero dropped events, ring-buffer overflows, restarts, unmonitored processes or sequence gaps.
Count of runs accepted as closed when any expected process lacks an exit, an expected child is missing, or child/parent exit ordering is invalid.
Count of runs accepted after joining process identities across different host boot or PID namespace contexts.
Count of runs accepted with duplicate identity tuples, orphan parents, cycles or invalid process incarnation fields.
95th percentile audit latency for a 10,000-process and 100,000-event synthetic upper-bound receipt pair on a declared reference host.
95th percentile audit report size for the same upper-bound lineage workload.
Fraction of exec event occurrences matched by process instance, per-process ordinal and exact executable-image SHA-256 digest.
Fraction of process instances whose exec ordinals are unique, contiguous from one and consistent between the independent oracle and observer receipt.
Fraction of clone events whose exact clone flags reconcile, with CLONE_THREAD excluded from the process-only profile rather than normalized as a process child.

gates.promotion_rule: All safety gates are mandatory and non-compensatory. Efficiency is evaluated only after every safety gate passes. No composite score is permitted to compensate for lineage loss or false closure.

statistical_protocol.clustering: Events, syscalls, retries and repeated process starts within one task attempt are not independent samples. Cluster by repository task lineage and host boot/PID namespace.
statistical_protocol.splits: Separate development, qualification and untouched confirmatory task lineages. Hold out workload templates and PID/namespace mutation strategies, not merely random event rows.
statistical_protocol.stopping: Preregister independent task attempt count, host/kernel strata, mutation generators, event-rate controls, retries, exclusions and confidence intervals before qualification.
